question.problem:
Starting with the standard Maclaurin expansion for ${e}^{x},$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion for
$\int x{e}^{-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
The series expansion of ${e}^{x}$ is

$$
{e}^{x}=1+x+\frac{1}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯\,.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-{x}^{2}$ in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-{x}^{2}} & =1+(-{x}^{2})+\frac{1}{2!}(-{x}^{2})^{2}+\frac{1}{3!}(-{x}^{2})^{3}+⋯ \\  & =1-{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply the series by $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x{e}^{-{x}^{2}} & =x\cdot (1-{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+⋯) \\  & =x-{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{5}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, integrating with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (x-{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{5}+⋯)\,\text{d}x \\  & =C+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{12}{x}^{6}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$
